steps.intent: Our objective is to renew UNDOF for six months while preserving the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement and affirming Syrian sovereignty, using balanced language that does not single out Israel and can secure consensus. The main difficulty will be retaining the call for the withdrawal of unauthorized military personnel and equipment from the area of separation and the area of limitation, which the United States and some Western members may seek to dilute. We expect a technical rollover to pass if the text remains anchored in resolution 2766 (2024) and the Secretary-General’s report.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate and appreciates the penholders’ efforts. However, the text should not remain silent on the Israeli incursion and attacks against Syrian territory; we therefore ask for explicit references to these violations and a clear call for withdrawal to the ceasefire line. Algeria can support the draft with these amendments.
messages.China: China supports the current draft and believes it provides a balanced basis for renewing UNDOF’s mandate. We welcome the references to Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, to full respect for the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, and to the withdrawal of unauthorized military personnel and equipment. China is prepared to vote in favour and calls on all Council members to maintain consensus.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports renewal of UNDOF's mandate and the balanced basis of the draft. We ask the penholders to make explicit that the 1974 Agreement remains in force and to strengthen OP3 so that all unauthorized forces, including those that entered the area of separation after 8 December 2024, withdraw immediately. We would also welcome a standard IHL/protection of civilians paragraph and an update to the outdated COVID-19 reference in OP8.
messages.France: France supports the renewal of UNDOF's mandate. The 1974 Disengagement Agreement remains in force and must be the basis for stability; the text should say so explicitly. We also need an unambiguous call for the withdrawal of all unauthorized forces, including Israeli forces that entered Syrian territory after 8 December 2024, and for full respect for Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity. Please add reporting on violations by all parties and on the status of withdrawals.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the renewal of UNDOF and considers the draft a balanced basis for consensus. We ask the penholder to add the principle of the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force in PP4, consistent with international law, and to strengthen OP17 so the Secretary-General reports on all violations and any unauthorized military presence in the areas of separation and limitation. These changes are important for the credibility of the 1974 Agreement and for effective Council oversight.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports renewal of UNDOF's mandate and welcomes the co-penholders' text, but we ask that it not lower the Council's earlier language on sovereignty, withdrawal and international humanitarian law. In particular, we seek an explicit reaffirmation that territory cannot be acquired by force and an OP3 that requires immediate withdrawal from unauthorized positions and restoration of the pre-8 December 2024 ceasefire line. We also ask to restore the call on all parties to the Syrian domestic conflict to cease military actions and respect international humanitarian law.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the renewal of UNDOF's mandate, but the draft must reflect the serious violations that have occurred since 8 December 2024. We ask the penholders to add an explicit reaffirmation of Syrian sovereignty over the occupied Golan and an operative demand for the immediate withdrawal of Israeli forces from the area of separation and all Syrian territory seized since that date. With these balancing amendments, Pakistan can support the text.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate through 31 December 2025 and welcomes the balanced text circulated by the penholders. The draft appropriately stresses respect for the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, the withdrawal of unauthorized military personnel and equipment, and the safety and freedom of movement of United Nations peacekeepers. We encourage the Council to maintain this consensus and to continue supporting UNDOF’s return to the area of separation as security conditions permit.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate and welcomes the balanced text circulated by the Russian Federation and co-sponsored by the United States. We particularly value the reaffirmation of sovereignty and territorial integrity, the call for withdrawal of unauthorized military personnel and equipment, and the strong emphasis on the safety and security of United Nations peacekeepers. We encourage all parties to fully respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement and to cooperate with UNDOF so that it can implement its mandate safely and return to its area of operations as soon as practicable.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone broadly supports the renewal of UNDOF's mandate and welcomes the draft's reaffirmation of Syrian sovereignty and territorial integrity and its call for the withdrawal of unauthorized military personnel and equipment. We ask the penholders to retain the previous consensus language calling on all parties to the Syrian domestic conflict to cease military actions and respect international humanitarian law, which is missing from this text. A unified Council message on protection of civilians and UN personnel remains essential.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the renewal of UNDOF's mandate and welcomes the draft's reaffirmation of Syria's sovereignty and the call to withdraw unauthorized forces. We ask the penholders to make that call explicit with regard to Israeli forces that have entered the area of separation and beyond since 8 December 2024. We also ask to reintroduce language on respect for international humanitarian law and the protection of civilians, which was included in resolution 2766 (2024).
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports renewal of UNDOF’s mandate and the Council’s continued attention to the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. However, the text should not avoid the Israeli incursion into the area of separation and Syrian territory after 8 December 2024. We request explicit reaffirmation of the inadmissibility of acquiring territory by force and a clear call for the withdrawal of unauthorized forces, including Israeli forces, from the area of separation and area of limitation. Somalia also asks that the preamble refer to the occupied Syrian Golan.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports renewal of UNDOF's mandate and welcomes the balanced text. We ask that OP3 make clear that all unauthorized forces, including Israeli forces that crossed the ceasefire line after 8 December 2024, must withdraw and that the 1974 Agreement remains in force. We also want the text to reflect the Secretary-General's reporting on all violations, including attacks by Hezbollah and other armed groups against Israeli positions and UNDOF personnel.
messages.United States of America: The United States, as a co-sponsor, supports the draft as presented. It provides a balanced renewal of UNDOF’s mandate and underscores the importance of full compliance with the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement by all parties. We urge all Council members to join consensus so that UNDOF can continue its vital work.

steps.summary: The revised text preserves consensus on renewing UNDOF while incorporating balanced language on the 1974 Agreement, withdrawal of unauthorized forces after 8 December 2024, IHL, and stronger reporting. It avoids explicit naming of Israel or Hezbollah, which should keep the United States and other permanent members from blocking the text, while retaining enough flexibility for most Council members to support renewal.

messages.Algeria: Algeria welcomes the penholder’s partial acceptance and supports renewing UNDOF, but the text must reflect the gravity of Israel’s violations of the 1974 Agreement. We ask that the draft explicitly identify Israeli forces in the withdrawal call, condemn Israel’s incursion, and demand an end to attacks on Syrian territory. These changes are consistent with resolution 2766 (2024) and Algeria’s longstanding position on Syrian sovereignty.
messages.China: China supports the revised draft and appreciates the co-penholders' efforts to preserve consensus. The text reflects China's key concerns on sovereignty, territorial integrity and the inadmissibility of acquiring territory by force, as well as the need for unauthorized forces to withdraw from the area of separation and limitation. China will vote in favour and calls on all parties to implement the resolution in good faith. No further changes are requested.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the current draft. It now clearly reaffirms that the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement remains in force, calls for the immediate withdrawal of unauthorized forces including those that entered after 8 December 2024, and incorporates international humanitarian law and humanitarian access. We will vote in favour.
messages.France: France welcomes the revision, in particular the reaffirmation that the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement remains in force and the call for withdrawal from the area of separation and area of limitation. To be consistent with the preamble and Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, OP3 should also cover all other Syrian territory occupied since 8 December 2024, including the Syrian side of Mount Hermon, and should require a return to positions held prior to 8 December 2024. France can support the renewal on that basis.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the revised draft and commends the penholders for incorporating the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force and for strengthening reporting on violations and unauthorized presence. The text upholds the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, UNDOF’s mandate and impartiality, and the safety and security of peacekeepers. Greece will vote in favour and urges all Council members to support a unified renewal of UNDOF’s mandate until 31 December 2025.
messages.Guyana: Guyana welcomes the penholder’s partial incorporation of our amendments, particularly the reaffirmation of the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force and the call for immediate withdrawal of unauthorized forces. To ensure OP3 is fully consistent with the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement and the preservation of the ceasefire line, we request the additional restoration language above. Guyana continues to support the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate and will not block the text, but this clarification remains important to our delegation.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan welcomes the partial acceptance of its earlier proposals and remains committed to renewing UNDOF's mandate. For our support, the text should clearly identify the forces that entered the area after 8 December 2024 and call for an end to Israeli strikes and incursions into Syrian territory. We also seek a new operative paragraph demanding withdrawal from all Syrian territory occupied since 8 December 2024, including Mount Hermon and Quneitra, in line with the principle that territory cannot be acquired by force.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the revised draft as a balanced consensus text and welcomes the co-sponsorship by the Russian Federation and the United States. We particularly value the reaffirmation of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, respect for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, the call for withdrawal of unauthorized forces, and the protection of civilians and UN personnel. We therefore encourage the Council to adopt the text without further changes and to renew UNDOF’s mandate until 31 December 2025.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate and welcomes the revised draft’s balanced provisions on sovereignty, the withdrawal of unauthorized forces, and the safety and security of peacekeepers. We have no further changes to request and encourage all Council members to support the text as it stands.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the current text and welcomes the restoration of the call on all parties to the Syrian domestic conflict to cease military actions and respect international humanitarian law. The draft appropriately stresses respect for the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, the withdrawal of unauthorized forces, and the safety and impartiality of UNDOF. We encourage the Council to speak with one voice in renewing UNDOF’s mandate.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia welcomes the partial incorporation of our proposals, especially the strengthened IHL language and the date-based withdrawal reference. We can support the renewal, but OP3 remains euphemistic given the scale of the Israeli incursion. We therefore ask that OP3 explicitly name Israeli forces and require their return to positions held before 8 December 2024.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports renewal of UNDOF’s mandate and welcomes the addition of general inadmissibility language, but the text remains ambiguous on the occupied Syrian Golan and on the scope of Israel’s incursion. We ask that PP4 explicitly refer to the occupied Syrian Golan and that OP3 call for the immediate withdrawal of Israeli forces from all Syrian territory occupied since 8 December 2024, including the area of separation, and demand that Israel cease further incursions. These changes are important for the Council to uphold international law and Syrian sovereignty.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: We welcome the revision and the date-based withdrawal language, which we can support. However, the text still does not explicitly condemn Hezbollah’s attacks against Israeli positions in the Golan Heights, and we continue to regard that as an important omission. We are ready to support renewal once this is reflected.
messages.United States of America: We appreciate the penholder's efforts and remain committed to renewing UNDOF's mandate. However, we cannot support a text that effectively demands Israeli withdrawal from the buffer zone by a specific date or implies unlawful territorial acquisition; these provisions must remain neutral and focused on all parties. With the deletion of the 8 December reference in OP3 and the softening of PP5, we can support the draft.

replies.France: partially accepted: general restoration of full compliance with the 1974 Agreement included, but no explicit 8 December or Mount Hermon reference due to balance and red lines.
replies.Guyana: partially accepted: preservation of the ceasefire line and restoration of compliance included, but no specific pre-8 December positions language.
replies.Pakistan: rejected: explicit naming of Israeli forces and a new withdrawal demand would undermine consensus and P5 support.
replies.Slovenia: rejected: explicit naming of Israeli forces was not included in order to maintain a balanced text.
replies.Somalia: rejected: occupied Syrian Golan reference and explicit withdrawal demand were not included to preserve consensus.
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: accepted: added preambular condemnation of attacks by Hezbollah and other armed groups against Israeli positions in the Golan Heights.
replies.United States of America: accepted: deleted the 8 December reference in OP3 and softened PP5 in line with the stated red line.

steps.summary: The revision preserves a neutral UNDOF renewal until 31 December 2025, removes the contentious 8 December temporal reference from OP3, and softens the territorial-acquisition language to secure US support. A preambular condemnation of Hezbollah attacks was added for the United Kingdom. The text is expected to obtain the required nine votes without a permanent-member veto, though several members seeking stronger language on Israeli forces are expected to abstain.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria has consistently supported UNDOF mandate renewals and will not block this technical renewal despite unresolved concerns. It will vote yes while publicly recording that the text does not explicitly name Israel’s violations or demand an end to its military attacks and incursion.
reasons.China: China supports renewing UNDOF’s mandate and the draft’s emphasis on the 1974 Disengagement Agreement, Syrian sovereignty, and ceasefire stability; it had already indicated support during negotiations.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark generally supports renewing UNDOF’s mandate and a balanced text emphasizing respect for the 1974 Agreement, protection of UN peacekeepers and international humanitarian law. As an elected member with no requested changes, Denmark would vote in favour and explain its support before the vote.
reasons.France: France supports the UNDOF mandate renewal to preserve a key stabilisation tool, consistent with its prior votes, but it will use its explanation to distance itself from the draft’s failure to explicitly demand withdrawal from areas entered after 8 December 2024, including Mount Hermon.
reasons.Greece: Greece supports UN peacekeeping, the 1974 Disengagement Agreement, and the draft’s balanced reaffirmation of sovereignty, ceasefire compliance, civilian protection, and UNDOF’s safety and mandate renewal. No Greek red lines were unmet, and Greece had already indicated support without requested changes.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana has consistently supported UNDOF mandate renewals and the 1974 Disengagement Agreement, and its key requested change was at least partially reflected in the compromise text. A yes vote is consistent with Guyana’s support for peacekeeping, sovereignty, and Council unity on this file.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan prioritizes renewal of UNDOF and consensus on peacekeeping, while using the explanation to register its principled opposition to Israeli occupation and disappointment that its amendments were rejected. It therefore supports the draft while pressing for explicit respect for Syrian sovereignty and withdrawal of unauthorized forces.
reasons.Panama: Panama supports UN peacekeeping and the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate, consistent with its prior votes and stated support for the draft. The statement reinforces respect for the 1974 Agreement, sovereignty, and civilian protection without opposing the penholders’ text.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported renewing UNDOF’s mandate and the draft reaffirms the 1974 Disengagement Agreement, peacekeeper safety, and respect for Syria’s sovereignty. As no ROK concerns remained, it is expected to vote in favour without a pre-vote statement.
reasons.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation is the penholder and co-sponsor of the draft, which reflects its priorities on UNDOF renewal, Syrian sovereignty, and full compliance with the 1974 Agreement. It would therefore vote in favour and explain its support before the vote.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone has consistently supported UNDOF mandate renewals and takes no issue with the draft; it would vote in favour to uphold the 1974 Agreement, ceasefire and UN peacekeeping. A brief explanation in favour aligns with its peacekeeping and sovereignty-focused foreign policy.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia consistently supports UNDOF mandate renewals and would not block the mission despite its rejected amendment on explicitly naming Israeli forces. It would vote yes while registering serious concerns about violations and calling for withdrawal.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia would support renewing UNDOF to preserve stability and consensus, but as an Arab League member it would use the explanation of vote to register its objection to Israeli occupation and incursions in Syrian territory. The rejected amendments make a yes-with-reservations statement appropriate rather than opposing the mission renewal.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK supports renewing UNDOF’s mandate and secured its key requested language condemning Hezbollah attacks, while the draft also reinforces the 1974 agreement and calls for withdrawal of unauthorized forces. Voting in favour is consistent with the UK’s Council record on UNDOF and its interest in regional stability.
reasons.United States of America: The United States co-sponsored the draft and its red-line change on OP3 was accepted, so the text is consistent with U.S. support for renewing UNDOF while avoiding an explicit temporal singling out of Israeli forces. It also includes language condemning Hezbollah attacks and backing Israel’s security interests.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of this resolution, because the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate is essential to preserving stability and preventing a dangerous vacuum in the area of separation. At the same time, we regret that the Council has not explicitly named the Israeli incursion and continuing violations of Syrian sovereignty and territorial integrity. The Israeli military presence in the area of separation is illegal under the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, and we reiterate our call for the immediate and unconditional withdrawal of all unauthorized forces, an end to attacks against Syrian territory, full respect for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the protection of civilians and United Nations personnel.
before.Denmark: Denmark votes in favour of renewing the mandate of UNDOF. The 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement remains essential for stability between Israel and Syria, and all parties must fully respect the ceasefire line, the area of separation and the integrity of United Nations peacekeeping operations. Denmark remains concerned by violations of the Agreement and by military activity that endangers civilians and United Nations personnel, and we call on all parties to exercise restraint, withdraw unauthorized forces, protect civilians and ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access. We strongly support UNDOF’s mandate, the safety and freedom of movement of its personnel, and the mission’s return to its area of operations as soon as conditions permit.
before.France: France will vote in favour of renewing UNDOF’s mandate, which remains essential to monitoring the ceasefire and supporting stability on the ground. We regret, however, that the Council has not explicitly called for the withdrawal of all unauthorized forces that entered the area of separation after 8 December 2024 and for an end to Israel’s occupation of Syrian territory beyond the 1974 line, including the Syrian side of Mount Hermon. France recalls that the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement remains binding, that the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria must be respected, and that unilateral actions cannot alter the status of the Golan Heights.
before.Greece: Greece votes in favour of the draft resolution. We welcome the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate and reaffirm that the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement must be fully respected by all parties. Greece underscores the need to respect Syria’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence, and the obligation to maintain the ceasefire, preserve the area of separation from unauthorized military activity, protect civilians, ensure unimpeded humanitarian access, and guarantee the safety, security and freedom of movement of United Nations personnel. All violations, by any party, must cease and be clearly reported. UNDOF must be allowed to implement its mandate and return to its positions as soon as conditions permit. We thank the troop-contributing countries and the Secretary-General for their continued efforts.
before.Guyana: Guyana thanks the penholders for their efforts and for the partial incorporation of our proposals. We will vote in favour of this resolution because renewing UNDOF’s mandate is essential to preserving the ceasefire and supporting stability in the area of operations. We reaffirm the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of Syria and all States in the region, and we stress the obligation of all parties to fully respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. We welcome the text’s call for the withdrawal of unauthorized military personnel and equipment and for the restoration of full compliance. At the same time, we regret that the resolution does not explicitly reflect the need to restore positions and the ceasefire line as they stood prior to 8 December 2024. We nevertheless support the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate and call on all parties to cease violations, protect civilians, ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and guarantee the safety, security and freedom of movement of United Nations personnel. Guyana remains committed to a just and durable peace on the basis of the relevant Security Council resolutions.
before.Pakistan: Mr. President, Pakistan will vote in favour of the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate, which remains essential for stability and for supporting the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. We do so despite our serious concern that the text does not expressly demand the immediate and unconditional withdrawal of Israeli forces from all Syrian territory occupied since 8 December 2024, including the Syrian side of Mount Hermon and Quneitra Governorate, nor explicitly condemn Israeli military strikes and incursions. We call for full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence, strict compliance with the ceasefire and the area of separation, protection of civilians, and unimpeded freedom of movement for United Nations peacekeepers. The acquisition of territory by force is inadmissible, and all unauthorized forces must withdraw.
before.Panama: Panama will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate and call on all parties to respect fully the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, to refrain from military activity in the area of separation, and to uphold the sovereignty and territorial integrity of States in the region. The safety and security of United Nations peacekeepers and the protection of civilians must remain central, and we urge constructive engagement to allow UNDOF to return to its area of operations as soon as conditions permit.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation votes in favour of the draft resolution it has submitted together with the United States. The text is balanced and reaffirms the continued force of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, and the need for strict compliance by all parties. We underscore that unilateral military actions and violations of the area of separation must cease, unauthorized forces must withdraw, and UNDOF must be able to operate safely and return to its area of operations. We therefore support the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate until 31 December 2025 and call on all parties to fully respect their obligations.
before.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone votes in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate and reaffirm the importance of full respect for the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, the ceasefire, and the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. We call on all parties to exercise restraint, withdraw unauthorized military personnel and equipment from the area of separation, protect civilians, and ensure the safety, security and freedom of movement of United Nations peacekeepers. Sierra Leone remains committed to the role of United Nations peacekeeping in supporting stability and a just and durable peace in the region.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the Secretary-General for the report and expresses its full support for UNDOF, Major General Anita Asmah and all troop-contributing countries. The 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement remains in force and must be fully respected by all parties. Slovenia remains deeply concerned by continued violations, including military activity in the area of separation and the area of limitation, and in particular by the presence of Israeli forces that entered Syrian territory after 8 December 2024. We regret that the draft before us does not explicitly call for their immediate withdrawal to positions held before that date. Respect for Syria’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence is essential, as is the protection of civilians and safe humanitarian access. Notwithstanding these shortcomings, Slovenia will vote in favour of the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate, which remains indispensable for stability and for the safety of United Nations personnel.
before.Somalia: Mr. President, Somalia will vote in favour of the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate, as the Force’s continued presence remains important for stability and for support to the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. At the same time, we regret that the draft does not expressly refer to the occupied Syrian Golan or demand the immediate withdrawal of Israeli forces from all Syrian territory occupied since 8 December 2024. We reaffirm that the Syrian Golan is occupied Syrian territory and that Israel’s incursions and military activities in the area of separation violate the Agreement and international law. We call for full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence, and we expect the Secretary-General’s reporting to address all violations and unauthorized military presence in the area of separation and the area of limitation. Somalia therefore supports this renewal while continuing to insist on full compliance by all parties and on a just and durable peace.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this draft resolution. UNDOF’s mandate remains essential to preserving the ceasefire and supporting stability between Israel and Syria. We welcome the incorporation of our proposed condemnation of attacks by Hezbollah and other armed groups against Israeli positions in the Golan Heights. We reiterate that the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement remains in force and must be fully respected by all parties, including through the immediate withdrawal of unauthorized military personnel and equipment from the area of separation. We call on all parties to ensure the safety, security and freedom of movement of United Nations personnel and to facilitate UNDOF’s return to its area of operations.
before.United States of America: The United States supports the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate. We welcome the Council’s clear condemnation of Hezbollah’s attacks against Israeli positions in the Golan Heights and our shared call on all parties to respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. UNDOF’s impartial presence and liaison role remain essential to preventing escalation. We urge all parties to ensure the safety, security, and freedom of movement of United Nations personnel and to avoid any actions that undermine the ceasefire line. The United States will vote in favour.

after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. We welcome its unanimous adoption and appreciate the efforts of the penholders in promoting Council consensus. The renewal of UNDOF’s mandate is important for maintaining stability in the area of separation and supporting the implementation of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement.

China stresses that the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement remains in force and must be fully respected by all parties. The sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of Syria must be respected. We call on all parties to exercise maximum restraint, cease military activity in the area of separation, withdraw unauthorized military personnel and equipment, and avoid any actions that could escalate tensions. The safety and security of United Nations peacekeepers must be guaranteed, and their freedom of movement and ability to implement their mandate must be fully ensured.

China supports a just and durable peace in the Middle East on the basis of the relevant Security Council resolutions and the principle of land for peace. We hope the parties will engage constructively so that UNDOF can return to its area of operations as soon as conditions permit. China will continue to support the role of United Nations peacekeeping and efforts to promote peace and stability in the region.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation, as a co-penholder of this resolution together with the United States, welcomes its unanimous adoption. The extension of UNDOF’s mandate until 31 December 2025 is a timely and necessary signal that the Security Council remains committed to preserving the ceasefire and supporting stability between Israel and the Syrian Arab Republic.

We thank Council members for their constructive engagement and their support for a balanced text. The resolution reaffirms the continued force of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement and resolution 338 (1973), stresses respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of the Syrian Arab Republic, and underscores that there should be no military forces, equipment or personnel in the area of separation other than those of UNDOF.

We note with concern the military activity and violations in the area of separation and the area of limitation. All parties must fully respect the Disengagement Agreement, cease unilateral actions, withdraw unauthorized military personnel and equipment, and ensure the safety, security and freedom of movement of United Nations peacekeepers. The Council must not allow the area of separation to become a zone of unregulated military presence or a platform for further escalation.

The Russian Federation calls on the parties to cooperate fully with UNDOF, including through its liaison function, and to create conditions for the mission’s return to its area of operations as soon as practicable. We will continue to follow the implementation of this resolution closely, including through the Secretary-General’s reporting.

Thank you.
after.United States of America: The United States welcomes the Security Council’s unanimous adoption of this resolution renewing the mandate of UNDOF. We thank the Secretary-General, Major General Asmah, and all troop-contributing countries for their service in a difficult and dangerous environment. This resolution rightly condemns attacks by Hezbollah and other armed groups against Israeli positions in the Golan Heights and calls on all parties to respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. UNDOF’s impartial presence and liaison role remain essential to preventing escalation and preserving the ceasefire. We urge all parties to ensure the safety, security, and freedom of movement of United Nations personnel, to avoid any military activity in the area of separation, and to facilitate UNDOF’s return to its area of operations as soon as conditions permit. The United States remains deeply concerned about the destabilizing role of Iran and its support for Hezbollah and other armed groups, and we will continue to defend Israel’s legitimate security interests. At the same time, all parties must exercise restraint and avoid actions that undermine the ceasefire line. We will continue to support UNDOF’s mandate and to hold accountable those who threaten peacekeepers or violate the Agreement.
